claims.text: The as-deposited or minimally annealed FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse-grained, non-recrystallized microstructure.
Extended high-temperature annealing of the FeNiCrCoCu coating induces dynamic recrystallization.
The annealing-induced recrystallization forms an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
Formation of the ultra-nanocrystalline layer increases near-surface grain-boundary density.
High grain-boundary density impedes dislocation slip in the coating.
Impeded dislocation slip causes the dominant microscopic deformation mode to shift toward deformation twinning.
The shift toward twinning produces a more uniform distribution of stress during sliding.
The proposed microstructural and deformation changes reduce localized deformation during sliding.
At approximately 600°C, the annealed coating will have a lower wear rate than the baseline coating.
At approximately 600°C, the annealed coating will have a lower friction coefficient than the baseline coating.
The annealed coating will show more near-surface deformation twinning and less dislocation-slip-dominated deformation than the baseline coating.
Overaging or grain coarsening beyond the proposed optimum may cause the predicted wear and deformation trends to fail.
